To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the esterification of quercetin-3-glucoside with long chain fatty acids enhances its lipophilicity and increases its antioxidant activity in lipid systems.
Q3G esterified with long chain fatty acids exhibited significantly higher inhibition in primary and secondary oxidation of PUFA-rich oil emulsions and Cu2+- and AAPH-induced LDL oxidation in vitro.
Q3G esterified with long chain fatty acids exhibited higher antioxidant activity in the oil-in-water model system than Q3G.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of long chain fatty acid esters of QG and their evaluation as antioxidants for preventing lipid oxidation in model systems of polyunsaturated fatty acid-rich fish oil and LDL.
the development and characterization of novel antioxidants, which are derived from natural plant sources and are esterified to long chain fatty acids.
the development of new antioxidants from flavonoid esters, which may provide an alternative to synthetic antioxidants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Q3G ester derivatives can be considered as effective antioxidants to prevent the oxidation of polyunsaturated lipids in food systems.
the esterified flavones were effective antioxidants in lipid oxidation model systems, and their applications can be further enhanced in food systems by the use of biocatalytic esterification.
the antioxidant activity of the Q3G ester derivatives is highly dependent on the type of fatty acid esterified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
esters of QG can be considered as promising antioxidant candidates for the protection of PUFA-rich foods and lipids from oxidation.
esterification of Q3G with long chain fatty acids enhanced its antioxidant properties and improved its applications in lipophillic food systems.
the antioxidant activity of Q3G can be enhanced by esterifying with fatty acids, especially with EPA, DHA, and ALA, which are poly-unsaturated and have a high number of double bonds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Q3G can be esterified to long chain fatty acids by lipase-catalysis and the resulting esters can be utilized as antioxidants for protection of lipids from oxidation.
esterification of Q3G with long chain fatty acids can improve its antioxidant activity against oxidation of lipids in aqueous and lipophilic systems.
Q3G esterification with long chain fatty acids can be used as an approach to improve the antioxidant activity of flavonoids in lipophilic systems.
